'''Céline Bœhm''' {{Post-nominals|country=AUS|FAA}} {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FInstP}} is a professor of [[particle physics]] at the [[University of Sydney]]. She works on [[astroparticle physics]] and [[dark matter]].

== Early life and education ==
Bœhm studied fundamental physics at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], graduating in 1997.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://sydney.edu.au/news/science/397.html?newsstoryid=16825|title=News {{!}} The University of Sydney|website=sydney.edu.au|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref> She joined [[École Polytechnique]], where she obtained a Master in Engineering in 1998.<ref name=":1" /> She earned the highest distinction for a postgraduate diploma in theoretical physics.<ref name=":1" /> She completed her PhD at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure in Paris]] in 2001, working with [[:fr:Pierre Fayet|Pierre Fayet]].{{citation needed|date=September 2018}} She worked on supersymmetry, in the 4-body decay of the stop particle. She studied light scalar [[top quark]] and [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetric]] dark matter and looked at collisional damping, which considers the impact of dark matter and [[Standard Model|standard model]] particles with the [[cosmic microwave background]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=C.|last2=Djouadi|first2=A.|last3=Drees|first3=M.|date=2000-07-12|title=Light Scalar Top Quarks and Supersymmetric Dark Matter|arxiv=hep-ph/9911496|journal=Physical Review D|volume=62|issue=3|article-number=035012|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.62.035012|bibcode=2000PhRvD..62c5012B|s2cid=15138751|issn=0556-2821}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ippp.dur.ac.uk/profile/cboehm|title=Celine Boehm {{!}} Institute for Particle Physics Phenomenology|website=www.ippp.dur.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-28|archive-date=2019-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401111530/https://www.ippp.dur.ac.uk/profile/cboehm}}</ref>

== Career and research==
In 2001 Bœhm joined [[Joseph Silk]] at the [[University of Oxford]]. Here she worked on [[light dark matter]] particles which couple to light [[W′ and Z′ bosons|Z′ bosons]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=C.|last2=Ensslin|first2=T. A.|last3=Silk|first3=J.|date=2004-03-01|title=Can annihilating Dark Matter be lighter than a few GeVs?|arxiv=astro-ph/0208458|journal=Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics|volume=30|issue=3|pages=279–285|doi=10.1088/0954-3899/30/3/004|bibcode=2004JPhG...30..279B|s2cid=119056668|issn=0954-3899}}</ref> She proposed new candidates for scalar dark matter, in the form of heavy fermions or light gauge bosons.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=C.|last2=Fayet|first2=P.|date=2004|title=Scalar Dark Matter candidates|arxiv=hep-ph/0305261|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=683|issue=1–2|pages=219–263|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2004.01.015|bibcode=2004NuPhB.683..219B|s2cid=17516917}}</ref> When the SPI spectrometer onboard [[INTEGRAL]] identified a 511 keV line in the [[Galactic Center]], Bœhm suggested that this could have been the signature of dark matter.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=Celine|last2=Hooper|first2=Dan|last3=Silk|first3=Joseph|last4=Casse|first4=Michel|date=2004-03-12|title=MeV Dark Matter: Has It Been Detected?|arxiv=astro-ph/0309686|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=92|issue=10|article-number=101301|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.101301|pmid=15089189|bibcode=2004PhRvL..92j1301B|s2cid=17988955|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> She has continued to search for new signatures of dark matter, including examining the GeV excess in the [[Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope]] data.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=Celine|last2=Dolan|first2=Matthew J.|last3=McCabe|first3=Christopher|last4=Spannowsky|first4=Michael|last5=Wallace|first5=Chris J.|date=2014-05-08|title=Extended gamma-ray emission from Coy Dark Matter|arxiv=1401.6458|journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics|volume=2014|issue=5|page=009|doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2014/05/009|bibcode=2014JCAP...05..009B|s2cid=119184166|issn=1475-7516}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lacroix|first1=Thomas|last2=Boehm|first2=Celine|last3=Silk|first3=Joseph|date=2014-08-08|title=Fitting the Fermi-LAT GeV excess: On the importance of including the propagation of electrons from dark matter|arxiv=1403.1987|journal=Physical Review D|volume=90|issue=4|article-number=043508|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.90.043508|bibcode=2014PhRvD..90d3508L|s2cid=55698259|issn=1550-7998}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boehm|first1=Celine|last2=Dolan|first2=Matthew J.|last3=McCabe|first3=Christopher|date=2014-07-22|title=A weighty interpretation of the Galactic Centre excess|arxiv=1404.4977|journal=Physical Review D|volume=90|issue=2|article-number=023531|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.90.023531|issn=1550-7998}}</ref> In 2004 Bœhm joined the Laboratoire d'Annecy-le-Vieux de Physique Théorique, where she was promoted to senior lecturer in 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/celineboehmlapth/|title=celineboehm@lapth|website=sites.google.com|access-date=2018-09-28}}{{Dead link|date=October 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> She was awarded the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] Bronze Medal.<ref name=":0" />

She looked at the analysis of the [[CoGeNT]] direct detection method, and found that it could have suffered from a large background.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Davis|first1=Jonathan H.|last2=McCabe|first2=Christopher|last3=Boehm|first3=Celine|date=2014-08-06|title=Quantifying the evidence for Dark Matter in CoGeNT data|arxiv=1405.0495|journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics|volume=2014|issue=8|page=014|doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2014/08/014|bibcode=2014JCAP...08..014D|s2cid=54532870|issn=1475-7516}}</ref> In 2015 Boehm was nominated as Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]]. She is the [[Principal investigator]] of the ''Theia'' mission, a space observatory which will allow Bœhm and her team to test the [[dark matter]] predictions that arise due to the [[Lambda-CDM model]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=The Theia Collaboration|last2=Boehm|first2=Celine|last3=Krone-Martins|first3=Alberto|last4=Amorim|first4=Antonio|last5=Anglada-Escude|first5=Guillem|last6=Brandeker|first6=Alexis|last7=Courbin|first7=Frederic|last8=Ensslin|first8=Torsten|last9=Falcao|first9=Antonio|date=2017-07-02|title=Theia: Faint objects in motion or the new astrometry frontier|arxiv=1707.01348}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ippp.dur.ac.uk/theia-meeting|title=Theia meeting {{!}} Institute for Particle Physics Phenomenology|website=www.ippp.dur.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-28|archive-date=2018-09-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180929194545/https://www.ippp.dur.ac.uk/theia-meeting}}</ref>

Boehm was made an [[Emmy Noether]] Fellow at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in 2016, where she continued to work on dark matter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/people/celine-boehm|title=Celine Boehm {{!}} Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|language=en|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Wonders of Physics|title=Dark Matter with Dr Celine Boehm|date=2016-05-09|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AzHArWpdg_I|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref> That year, she was promoted to Professor in the [[Institute for Particle Physics Phenomenology]] at  [[Durham University]]. She gave a [[TED (conference)|TED]] talk, ''The Invisible is All What Matters'', at Durham in 2017.<ref>{{Citation|last=TEDx Talks|title=The Invisible is All What Matters {{!}} Dr. Celine Boehm {{!}} TEDxDurhamUniversity|date=2017-01-26|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UYk_pjkFobM|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref> Alongside her work in astroparticle physics, she works on non-crystallographic [[Coxeter group]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dechant|first1=Pierre-Philippe|last2=Boehm|first2=Celine|last3=Twarock|first3=Reidun|date=2013|title=Affine extensions of non-crystallographic Coxeter groups induced by projection|arxiv=1110.5228|journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics|volume=54|issue=9|page=093508|doi=10.1063/1.4820441|bibcode=2013JMP....54i3508D|s2cid=59469917|issn=0022-2488}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dechant|first1=Pierre-Philippe|last2=Boehm|first2=Celine|last3=Twarock|first3=Reidun|date=2012-07-20|title=Novel Kac-Moody-type affine extensions of non-crystallographic Coxeter groups|arxiv=1110.5219|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical|volume=45|issue=28|article-number=285202|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/45/28/285202|bibcode=2012JPhA...45B5202D|s2cid=44541666|issn=1751-8113}}</ref> She led the dark matter working package of the [[Euclid Consortium]]. In 2017 Bœhm spent two months as a visiting professor at [[Columbia University]], as well as working at the [[Paris Observatory]]. She proposed using [[Circular polarization|circular polarisation]] to study dark matter and neutrinos.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bœhm|first1=Céline|last2=Degrande|first2=Céline|last3=Mattelaer|first3=Olivier|last4=Vincent|first4=Aaron C.|date=2017|title=Circular polarisation: a new probe of dark matter and neutrinos in the sky|journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics|language=en|volume=2017|issue=5|page=043|doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2017/05/043|issn=1475-7516|arxiv=1701.02754|bibcode=2017JCAP...05..043B|s2cid=54747614}}</ref> She joined the University of Sydney as Head of School for physics in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/celine-boehm-to-head-sydney-physics-school/news-story/1365761d72932b8c822dacf78817b4ed|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230806162142/https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/celine-boehm-to-head-sydney-physics-school/news-story/1365761d72932b8c822dacf78817b4ed|url-status=live|archive-date=August 6, 2023|title=Subscribe to The Australian {{!}} Newspaper home delivery, website, iPad, iPhone & Android apps|website=The Australian|language=en|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Bœhm has written for [[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/celine-boehm-185474|title=Celine Boehm|website=The Conversation|date=19 August 2015 |language=en|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref> She has taken part in [[Pint of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pintofscience.co.uk/event/science-on-the-grand-scale|title=Science on the Grand Scale|website=Pint of Science|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-09-28}}</ref>

Bœhm was elected a [[List of fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celine Boehm |url=https://science.org.au/about-us/academy-fellows/discover-our-fellows/celine-boehm |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref>
